title: Tenant isolation: an operator from another tenant cannot decide, and no item state changes
risk: An operator of tenant T2 approves a T1 campaign, which is both a cross-tenant control failure and an unreviewed commercial commitment.
preconditions: Namespace gov-apv-<case_id>-<worker_id>; approval queue seeded from fixtures/offline/governance.json.
Operator identities and roles resolved from the fixture operator registry; every decision goes through POST /api/v1/approvals/{id}/decision, the only approval route.
APV-CAMP-15 belongs to T1; the acting session is authenticated as OP-APPROVER-T2 in tenant T2.

steps.action: Submit the decision with the T2 session against the T1 item
steps.expected: The gateway refuses with 403 or 404; the response body reveals no T1 payload fields.
Status is still AWAITING_HUMAN with the same payload_hash and no decided_at.

steps.action: Attempt the same request with the tenant header forged to T1
steps.expected: The forged header does not grant access because the session's verified tenant is authoritative; refusal repeats.
The cross-tenant attempts are recorded with the acting tenant and the target item, and no execution row exists.

assertions: Zero state changes on the foreign item; the payload hash and status are byte-identical before and after.
No T1 payload field is disclosed in the refusal response.
A forged tenant header cannot override the verified session tenant.
Each refused attempt is audited with the mismatch, so the control failure is visible if it ever succeeds.
forbidden: Resolving the item by id alone without a tenant predicate.
Leaking the target payload in an error message.
Trusting the client-supplied tenant header over the verified session.
evidence: T1 item state and payload hash before/after.
Audit rows with the acting and target tenants.
cleanup: Delete gov- refusal audit copies after export; the T1 item is left in its original pending state or cancelled through a legitimate T1 operator.
automation: Real tenant-scoped authorization and gateway middleware under test; the tenant contexts are separate authenticated sessions. The forged-header probe is issued at the HTTP boundary, not inside the service.
note: Generated acceptance specification. Plain specification, not an executable test; no application runtime exists, so the status is NOT_RUN.
